summary: AI chip policy peaks today: the closed cloud-rental loophole hit Asian chip stocks overnight, and Nvidia reports its first quarter under an interim CEO after the close. The Fed path is hardening: Musalem now sees 'several' hikes by spring after hot core retail sales and import prices, with the minutes due Nov 18. The Gulf flared again: the IRGC claims a strike on a US radar in Bahrain (CENTCOM says intercepted), lifting oil 1.5%.

risks.title: Fed hiking path and Fed leadership (Chair Warsh)
risks.status: Held 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 (Hammack and Cook dissented for a hike); October CPI +0.4% / core +0.3% m/m vs +0.3% / +0.2% (third straight 0.3% core; shelter +0.3%); Waller had set ~0.3% core as the bar for considering 50bp; Logan wants 'at least two more' hikes; Nov 12 claims 200K (prior 191K); Daly (more hikes likely) and Hammack (gradual, no 50bp needed) on Nov 12; Nov 13 October PPI +0.3% m/m vs +0.4% expected, 6.5% y/y vs 6.6%, core +0.3% in line; Daly said Nov 13 the Fed will 'in all likelihood' need to raise rates; Nov 16 Empire State 7.8 vs 16.7 expected; Nov 17: October retail sales +0.2% (in line) but ex-autos +0.6% vs +0.4%, import prices +1.1% vs +0.7%; Musalem (2028 voter) said the economy will likely need 'several' hikes before spring 2027 (up to four, real rate to 2-2.5%); Waller 09:10, Hammack 09:30, Williams 14:25 today; FOMC minutes Nov 18 14:00, Jefferson Nov 19 09:25, Cook Nov 20 12:15; November CPI lands after the Dec 9 decision
risks.odds: Dec 9 hike 100%, implied 4.18% (+30bp) (fed funds futures, Nov 17); FedWatch ~95% 25bp / ~4% 50bp (Quackonomist citing CME, Nov 17), down from 9-13% 50bp after PPI
risks.market_pricing: Nov 17 09:16: 13-week 4.15% (3-month high), 5Y 4.964% (+2.9bp), 10Y 5.147% (+2.6bp, +16bp in 5 days), 30Y 5.485%; DXY 103.62 (3-month high); gold 3,862 near a 3-month low
risks.impact: A hot PPI or 50bp signal pushes the 10Y toward 5.31% and hits long-duration tech, small caps and housing; a soft PPI and a 25bp-and-pause message would ease yields and help rate-sensitive groups

risks.title: AI / chip policy: Nvidia leadership crisis, export controls and data-center backlash
risks.status: Nov 12 (8:48 ET): Nvidia said Jensen Huang resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately after a board probe of reported affairs (one with a woman US reports link to Chinese intelligence); CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO, Harvey Jones the first board chair, a CEO search is under way; Q3 results still Nov 17. NVDA opened about -14%, pared to about -7%. Earlier: The Information reported $7.5B of Nvidia hardware reached China via a Huang-linked network; the White House is reportedly weighing new export controls on advanced Nvidia chips; post-midterm data-center moratorium pledges (Texas). CoreWeave beat Q3 and raised guidance (backlog $132.5B) but fell 9-13% on Nov 12; Nebius -19%. Nov 13: the sell-off broadened: AMD -9.8%, Broadcom -5 to -6% (Rothschild & Co Redburn downgrade to neutral), Marvell -8%, Micron -5%, NVDA -4% (sixth weekly loss, ~-14% on the week); Cerebras +16% on a surprise profit; AMAT slightly up after beating. Nov 16: CNBC reports the Commerce Department issued a rule closing the loophole that let Chinese firms rent Nvidia compute in other countries (earlier reports called it a draft; text not yet published); NVDA about -4% pre-market after -13% last week, Mizuho target cut to $220 and UBS to $240; MU, INTC, AMD, DELL -5%+ pre-market; Advantest -10%, SK Hynix -5.6% overnight; Anthropic IPO expected this week ($70-78 range, ~$1.4T valuation). Nov 16 close: PHLX semis -5.28%, NVDA -4.1%. Nov 17: Kospi -2.6%, Taiex -2.3%, ASML -2.8% on the curbs; Commerce now requires licenses for advanced AI chip purchases by data-center operators in several countries; Nvidia formed a National Security and Export Control Committee, its general counsel testifies privately to House committees Dec 2; Trump said he 'would not mind' Huang's return (Polymarket ~16%); options imply ~8% on Nvidia's Q3 tonight, BofA 10-15% odds the guide is withdrawn; NVDA +1.2% pre-market; Anthropic pricing expected Wed, trading Thu
risks.market_pricing: Nov 17 09:16: SOXX pre-market 143.73 (+1.8%) after -5.41% Monday; QQQ 663.72 (+0.3%, below its 200-day 681.41); SMH -11.4pp vs SPY over 1 month, -15.6pp over 3 months; VIX 22.92 with VIX9D 23.15 above it
risks.impact: Formal export controls, a messy succession or a weak Nov 17 report would extend the AI de-rating and drag cap-weighted indexes; a clean Nov 17 report with intact guidance would show the business is separate from the governance issue and spark a short-covering rally

risks.title: US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz closure
risks.status: Nov 12 (8:15 ET): Trump posted 'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed', claimed the US holds Iran's money and 'their Strait', and told Vance to focus on crime in Democratic-run states, a day after the WSJ said Vance was weighing direct talks with Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei (Rezaei denies talks). Strikes have largely subsided into a stalemate; Qatar-led mediation and a Qatari-Pakistani reopening plan had been gaining momentum; the interim deal is unsigned and the blockade remains. Nov 13: Iran's IRGC says an LNG tanker hit a naval mine and exploded in Hormuz, and Iran's army says two more tankers hit mines east of the strait (Iranian claims, not independently verified). Nov 16: the IRGC says two more tankers hit mines, after six tanker fires Sunday-Monday (Reuters could not verify); the US military says the recognized transit routes were cleared of mines; the IEA (Nov 13) now sees a Q4 oil surplus as Middle East exports recover. Nov 17: the IRGC says it struck a US radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base (CENTCOM: drones intercepted, no damage); Iran's navy claims a supertanker and an LNG carrier hit mines in Hormuz; Tehran threatened civilian infrastructure near US or Israeli bases; Qatar says mediation continues; Vance says the campaign won't become a two-year commitment; Iraq resumed Kirkuk-Ceyhan exports
risks.odds: US-Iran ceasefire holds to Dec 31: 25% (Polymarket via ScanX, early Nov); no fresh reading found
risks.market_pricing: Nov 17 09:16: Brent 93.82 (+1.5%), WTI 87.11 (+1.6%) after Monday's ~-4%; Brent -14.4% over 1 month; OVX 50.3 (Nov 13)
risks.impact: A collapse of diplomacy or renewed strikes would send Brent back above $100-110 and add to inflation and hike pricing; a signed deal reopening Hormuz would push Brent toward the low $80s and help consumers, transports and rate-sensitive stocks while hurting energy and defense

risks.title: China-Taiwan tensions and chip export controls / tariffs
risks.status: The White House is reportedly considering new export controls on Nvidia's advanced chips (Nov 10, not officially confirmed); the Huang resignation has a China-intelligence angle that raises the odds of congressional scrutiny of chip-China ties; Taiwan curbed short selling and readied a stabilization fund on Nov 9; Chinese live-fire drills in mid-October; a report says US tariffs on Chinese chips are delayed to June 2027 (unconfirmed). Nov 17: Trump is in Manila for a Quad summit before APEC in Shenzhen, where a Trump-Xi meeting (possibly with Putin) is expected this week (unconfirmed); SCMP reports both sides extended suspensions of some trade restrictions ahead of it; Taiex -2.3% and Kospi -2.6% on the new US chip curbs
risks.market_pricing: SMH -15.8% over 3 months (-13.5pp vs SPY); SOXX 30% below its 52-week high
risks.impact: New export curbs or a Taiwan blockade drill would hit semis first; a trade thaw or no new rules after the Nvidia exit would help a rebound

risks.title: US government funding / shutdown risk
risks.status: The stopgap signed in early September funds the government through Dec 11; the House has passed 3 of 12 FY2027 bills (all 12 cleared committee) while Senate appropriations are deadlocked; the fight moves to a lame-duck session before the new Democratic Congress; no November deal reported
risks.impact: A December lapse would delay economic data (including releases the Fed needs) and dent Q4 growth; a full-year deal or a clean CR into the new Congress removes it

risks.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping
risks.status: A Houthi attack reportedly damaged Aramco offices in Riyadh (reported Nov 9, not confirmed elsewhere); Saudi-coalition operations against the Houthis; Saudi Arabia warned its Yanbu Red Sea oil hub could be targeted (Nov 6); no new incident found Nov 11-12
risks.market_pricing: No visible Red Sea premium shift; Brent moves are driven by Iran headlines
risks.impact: A hit on Saudi export infrastructure (Yanbu, the Red Sea alternative to Hormuz) would be a major oil shock; calm keeps the focus on Iran diplomacy

risks.title: OPEC+ output policy
risks.status: Nov 1: OPEC+ kept output targets unchanged through December; next meeting Nov 29; Goldman's December Brent forecast is $105 (2027 average $88)
risks.market_pricing: Brent 93.76, well below Goldman's $105 December forecast
risks.impact: A surprise increase would be bearish for oil and energy stocks; continued restraint keeps a floor under oil if an Iran deal reopens supply

risks.title: Israel government formation after the Oct 27 election
risks.status: Herzog handed Gadi Eisenkot the mandate on Nov 8 after 67 recommendations vs 46 for Netanyahu; Eisenkot has 28 days (extendable by 14) and says he is open to including Netanyahu; Arab-led parties back him from outside; Netanyahu stays caretaker PM and pushes for a unity government
risks.impact: An Eisenkot-led or unity government would likely be more cautious on Iran and Gaza (mildly bearish oil and defense); a failed mandate or a new election extends caretaker uncertainty

risks.title: Russia-Ukraine war and peace talks
risks.status: US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi (Nov 10-11), the first trilateral round since February, focused on security guarantees; Russia sent a higher-level delegation; no outcome reported yet; local truce in one town since Oct 27
risks.odds: Peace talks by Dec 31 90%, ceasefire by Dec 31 9.5%, by Mar 31 2027 23.5% (Polymarket via Rio Times, early Nov)
risks.impact: Real progress would be mildly bearish for defense and European gas; a collapse keeps the defense theme supported

risks.title: US midterm elections: divided government
risks.status: Resolved Nov 3-4: Democrats won the House and Senate; the new Congress sits in January; Republicans including Vance blame the Iran war for the losses; Trump is now redirecting Vance to domestic issues
risks.odds: Resolved (pre-vote: Democrats Senate 73%, prediction markets via Yahoo Finance Nov 3)
risks.market_pricing: Nov 4: Dow ~+2%, S&P +1.1%; homebuilders +6.4%, defense lower
risks.impact: Gridlock limits new fiscal policy; oversight of tariffs, defense, AI and the Iran war rises; the risk is now in specific sectors rather than the index
